html:
Numidia was an ancient Berber kingdom in North Africa, covering most of what is now northern Algeria and parts of Tunisia. It is shown here in 100 BCE.

It began as two realms: the Massylii in the east and the Masaesyli in the west. During the Second Punic War, Masinissa of the eastern kingdom sided with Rome, and after the war he ruled all Numidia from Cirta. In a reign of over fifty years he settled nomads as farmers and kept nibbling at the lands of Carthage, which helped bring on the war that destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE.

His grandson Jugurtha murdered his way to the throne and bribed Roman senators. Rome fought him in the Jugurthine War of 112 to 106 BCE, which made the name of Gaius Marius. The last great king, Juba I, sided with Pompey in Caesar's civil war. After Caesar won at Thapsus in 46 BCE, Juba killed himself and Numidia became a Roman province.
sum: Numidia was an ancient Berber kingdom in North Africa, covering most of what is now northern Algeria and parts of Tunisia. It is shown here in 100 BCE.
